2.text: clean--or, "faultless." weigheth--or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty (Pro 21:2; Pro 24:12).

3.text: (Compare Margin). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

4.text: for himself--"for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil (Psa 49:5; Jer 17:18); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.

6.text: By mercy and truth--that is, God's (Psa 85:10); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon. purged--expiated (as in Lev 16:33; Isa 27:9, Hebrew).

10.text: The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

11.text: are the Lord's . . . his work--that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.

12.text: Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.

13.text: A specification of the general sentiment of Pro 16:12.

14.text: This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death (Kg1 2:25), can be appeased by the wise.

15.text: light of . . . countenance--favor (Psa 4:6). life--preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable. the latter rain--fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable (Deu 11:14).

17.text: The highway--A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil. keepeth--observes.

18.text: (Compare Pro 15:33). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence a fall--literally, "sliding."

19.text: divide the spoil--that is, conquer. Avoid the society of the proud (Jam 4:6).

20.text: handleth a matter--wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare Pro 13:13). trusteth--(Compare Psa 2:12; Psa 118:8-9).

21.text: wise in heart--who rightly consider duty. sweetness of the lips--eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

22.text: Understanding--or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing (Pro 13:14), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.

23.text: The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.

24.text: (Compare Pro 15:26). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.

26.text: Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

27.text: ungodly man--(Compare Pro 6:12). diggeth up evil--labors for it. in his lips . . . fire--His words are calumniating (Jam 3:6).

30.text: He shutteth his eyes--denoting deep thought (Psa 64:6). moving his lips--or, "biting his lips"--a determined purpose (Pro 6:13).

31.text: (Compare Pro 20:29). if--or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in Pro 3:16; Pro 4:10, that piety is blessed with long life.

32.text: (Compare Pro 14:29). taketh a city--that is, by fighting.

33.text: Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God. Next: Proverbs Chapter 17
